**Moving an agent tool on no longer means rebuilding the base image: the daemon updates Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and the rest in place, in the background. Agent rows get a right-click menu, the storage pool indicator breaks down what AgentBox uses on disk, the top bar's usage meter follows the Claude account you're looking at, Settings and a project's Overview get one layout, and the agents' desktop gets a modern dock and clearer recordings.**

## What's new

- **Agent tools update in place.** The tools in the agents' base image — Claude Code, Codex,
  OpenCode, the GitHub CLI, the ACP adapters and the rest — are now pinned apart from the image
  itself. When a new AgentBox moves one on, the daemon updates them in the existing base in the
  background when it starts, and Setup shows "Updating agent tools…" meanwhile. Agents keep being
  made from the old base until the update is done. If it fails, the base is left as it was, and
  Setup says why and offers the rebuild; the daemon never starts a rebuild on its own.
- **Right-click an agent.** Every agent row — the rail, the agents list on Home and a project's
  Agents tab — has a context menu: open its chat or terminal, start, stop, pause or resume, retire,
  copy its branch name, open its pull request, or destroy it. Shift+F10 and the context-menu key
  open it too.
- **What's on disk.** Clicking **Storage pool** in the top bar shows what AgentBox uses on disk:
  agent machines, the base image and saved bases, worktrees, media, the state database and the
  daemon log, per project where that applies, largest first, with a total.
- **The usage meter follows the open page.** The top bar's usage meter shows the Claude account
  the page you're on spends: the default account on Home, the project's account on a project, and
  the agent's own account on an agent. Its tooltip says which account it shows and why. It's
  hidden for Codex and OpenCode agents, which don't report their usage.
- **One layout for settings.** Settings and a project's Overview line every setting up the same
  way, name and help on the left and the control on the right. Settings' tabs are grouped as Lead,
  New agents, Every agent and This app; a project's settings are split into New agents, Project
  chat and Accounts. Every setting does what it did before.
- **A quieter right rail.** The rail no longer shows what agents report, or unread counts. Rows
  keep the name, status, pull request, CPU and branch, and an agent waiting on you says **Asks you
  something** until you answer. Credential requests are still cards in the chats.
- **Pull request authors.** A project's pull requests list shows who opened each one.
- **The agents' desktop.** A modern dock at the bottom of the screen with launchers for the
  browser, file manager and terminal that raise a window already open instead of starting another.
  Recordings made with `agentbox media record start --input desktop` show a ripple where the
  pointer clicks and one caption for the keys pressed, grouping shortcuts and typed words.
- **New agents default to 2 CPU cores**, instead of every core but two, on any installation where
  the default was never set. A value you chose is kept.
- **Anonymous feature-usage stats.** Once a day, with the update check it already made, AgentBox
  sends how many times each feature was used (like `agent.create.claude: 3`) and nothing else: no
  names, paths, repositories, models or anything you typed. Turn it off in **Settings →
  Environment → Share anonymous usage stats**; anything that turns the update check off —
  its switch, `AGENTBOX_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` — turns this off too.
- **Security policy.** The repository has a [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/blob/v0.3.0/SECURITY.md):
  report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub.
- **Faster releases.** The release workflow builds Linux, Windows and the Mac in parallel.

## Fixes

- **A new project's chat can have its model, effort, context window and mode chosen before its
  first message.** In 0.2.0 those menus stayed empty until the chat had been used once, and a model
  chosen while the session was starting could be shown but never reach the tool.
- **Opus offers a 1M context window again.** In 0.2.0, once a chat on a Claude model compacted at
  200k, that size was remembered as the model's window, and Settings and `create_agent` only
  offered 200k from then on. Remembered windows under 1M are dropped once, on upgrade.
- **The desktop app builds on a Mac-hosted agent's worktree.** `npm --prefix desktop run build`
  failed with EACCES there in 0.2.0.

## What went wrong

- **The project chat's settings.** Those menus come from the chat's running session, and a project
  chat only started its session on the first message. It now starts when the chat is opened, and a
  model chosen before the session is ready is sent once it is.
- **The 1M window.** Claude Code reports a session's size capped at the size it compacts at, and
  AgentBox took that capped size for the model's window. It now ignores a size equal to the compact
  window.
- **The Mac build.** Node's `fs.cpSync` wrote a broken copy on the Lima VM's virtiofs mount; the
  build now copies files one by one.

## Install

```bash
chmod +x AgentBox-0.3.0-x86_64.AppImage
./AgentBox-0.3.0-x86_64.AppImage
```

Or, on Debian/Ubuntu, `sudo apt install ./AgentBox-0.3.0-amd64.deb`; on Arch, `sudo pacman -U
AgentBox-0.3.0-x64.pacman`. On a Mac, open the `.dmg` and drag AgentBox into Applications, then see
**Known limitations** below. On Windows, run the installer or the portable `.exe`. See the README's
[Install](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/blob/v0.3.0/README.md#install) for the rest.

**Upgrading from 0.2.0:** the agents' base image changed once more, so Settings asks you to rebuild
it (`agentbox image build`). Agents made before the rebuild keep working on the old image. From
here on, a release that only moves an agent tool updates the base in place instead.

## Known limitations

- **The storage popover's machine sizes** come from Incus's volume usage, which hasn't yet been
  checked against a real machine's disk; if they look wrong on yours, please
  [report it](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/issues).
- **The usage meter** only covers Claude Code: Codex and OpenCode don't report their limits.
- The rest are unchanged since
  [0.2.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.2.0), including the alpha, ad hoc
  signed Mac app, and [0.1.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.1.0): Windows is
  alpha too.
